text: Russell's paradox arises from the set R = {x : x ∉ x}. What contradiction does it produce?
choices: R is simultaneously finite and infinite
R equals its own power set
R ∈ R if and only if R ∉ R
R has no elements yet is non-empty
explanation: Asking whether R (the set of all sets that are not members of themselves) belongs to itself yields R ∈ R ⟺ R ∉ R, an outright contradiction, showing that unrestricted comprehension is inconsistent. The other options are not what the paradox derives.
